questions.question: Write the word equation and balanced chemical equation for magnesium burning in oxygen, and describe two observations.
questions.expected_answer: Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide; 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. The ribbon burns with a very bright white light and leaves a white powder.

questions.question: Explain why steel wool burns in a Bunsen flame but an iron nail does not.
questions.expected_answer: Steel wool has thin strands with a very large surface area in contact with air, so many iron atoms meet oxygen at once and heat does not escape quickly; the nail has a small surface area, so the reaction is too slow to burn.

questions.question: 2,4 g of magnesium is burnt and 4,0 g of product forms. Explain the increase in mass using the conservation of atoms.
questions.expected_answer: Oxygen atoms from the air combine with the magnesium atoms; no atoms are created. The extra 4,0 − 2,4 = 1,6 g is the mass of oxygen that combined, which was not weighed at the start.
